headline: NYC opens walk-in jobs center for public-service careers
dek: The new Jobs NYC Center in Lower Manhattan will offer career guidance, civil-service help, hiring halls and workshops beginning Oct. 5.
body: New York City officials opened a permanent Jobs NYC Center in Lower Manhattan on Monday, creating a walk-in hub where residents can get help finding and applying for public-service jobs.

The center at 2 Lafayette Street was developed by the Department of Small Business Services and the Department of Citywide Administrative Services. It will offer career counseling, guidance on civil-service exams, agency hiring halls, job fairs, workshops and recruitment support for city agencies and other public-sector partners.

Regular walk-in hours are scheduled to begin Oct. 5. The center will also host panels and training for city employees seeking promotions or other career advancement, while its street-level space will be used for workforce-development events and networking.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani marked the launch by swearing in 17 new members of the NYC Business Express Service Team, which helps entrepreneurs navigate city permits, licenses and inspections. The city said the team members were hired through an August hiring hall held during the center's soft launch.

The Jobs NYC initiative has helped 47 city agencies and public institutions recruit since 2024, according to the Mayor's Office. The new location gives the effort a fixed site for connecting job seekers with openings and explaining the city's hiring process.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: NYC Opens Jobs Center for Public-Service Careers
